Can you provide that or connect us to a short internal blurb we can share? We need it by EOD Tuesday for our procurement review.

- Cross-border transfers note and safeguards (SCCs, encryption, access controls)

Thanks — drafting below and attaching a text file with the initial phrasing (privacy-lite-card_v1.txt). Mina: I left two bracketed Qs where I need confirmation about bursting and default routing.

DRAFT (v1) — plain-language card (2 sentences + 3 bullets):

"Redwood Inference's Hosted API processes customer-provided prompts and model outputs to generate responses; we do not use customer data to train models and we retain only short-lived telemetry needed to operate the service. When customers select regional residency options we pin requests to that region; otherwise requests may be routed across regions to meet latency and capacity needs. [Confirm: is phrasing ok re: "routed across regions" vs "may be routed to compatible regions"]"

Key points:
- Cross-border transfers: We protect transfers with standard contractual clauses and encryption in transit; customers can request region-locking for residency-sensitive workloads.
- Subprocessors: We rely on major cloud infrastructure providers (compute, storage, logging) and a small set of CDN/telemetry partners; a current subprocessor list and updates are published in our subprocessor map.
- DPA & details: Full DPA language, subprocessor list, and data handling docs are available at [link to DPA/subprocessors map].

Questions/notes for Mina:
- Is it OK to say "we do not use customer data to train models" for all Hosted API tiers? (I believe yes for hosted but flag if any edge cases).
- Do we want to offer a one-line fallback for customers requesting contractual transfer safeguards beyond SCCs?

I attached privacy-lite-card_v1.txt and a Word doc I can iterate to produce a final .docx for Acme if this looks good.

-Laura

Subject: Re: Quick ask: short privacy blurb for procurement

Alex / Taylor — thanks for the clear ask and timeline. Below is a short, publishable card you can paste into your vendor packet. I copied our privacy lead Mina on the thread for any final nitpicks.

FINAL PUBLISHABLE CARD (one paragraph + bullets):

Redwood Inference's Hosted API processes customer-provided requests and returns model-generated responses; we do not use customer prompts or responses to train our models and we retain only short-lived telemetry required to run the service. Customers can choose a residency option to keep traffic in a specific region; if residency is not selected, requests may be routed to compatible regions to maintain low latency and availability.

Highlights:
- Cross-border transfers and safeguards: Transfers are covered by standard contractual clauses where required and protected by encryption in transit; customers with stricter residency needs can request region-locking.
- Subprocessors: We employ major cloud infrastructure providers for compute and storage, and a limited set of CDN/telemetry partners; an up-to-date subprocessor map is published for customers.
- Where to find the DPA: Full DPA language, the subprocessor list, and data handling details are available here: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cAcmePrivacyDraft

If you want this as a Word file to drop into your packet, I can send a .docx. Please also let me know if procurement wants a one-sentence legal caveat line.

Thanks —
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
